mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average by more than 1.5 percentage points when inflation remains above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures that prompt equity market participants to anticipate higher corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with rising unemployment, the 60-day forward return is negative or no better than the 5-day average (p-value > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly increase in HOUST retail sales exceeding 2% suggests strengthening consumer demand, which elevates expected corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of elevated inflation or negative GDP growth, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below -1% indicates softening supply constraints, lowering production costs and boosting investor confidence, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 100 days, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 70% of INDPRO declines exceeding -1%.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for three consecutive months, the persistent low-rate environment is interpreted as a deflationary bias that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, the 60-day forward return is negative or indistinguishable from a high-rate environment (p-value > 0.05 in regime-adjusted regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% after a sustained rise suggests labor market softening, reducing wage growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% after a 4-month upward trend
failure_condition: During periods of rising employment, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A two consecutive months of RSAFS retail sales declines exceeding -3% indicate weakening demand, which compresses earnings growth expectations and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by more than 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In high-growth regimes, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP demand index) shows a monthly increase exceeding 2% in a supply-constrained regime (as indicated by INDPRO < 95), it suggests pent-up demand that temporarily boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by more than 2% and INDPRO < 95 in the current month
failure_condition: In periods of excess supply (GDPC1 < INDPRO + 2%), the 20-day forward return is negative or no better than baseline (p-value > 0.05).
